questions.question_text: Structural brain imaging studies have been used to elucidate the neurobiology of mood disorders. Which ONE of the following abnormalities has NOT been shown in MRI studies of patients with major depression?

options.text: Decreased grey matter volume of the subgenual pre-frontal cortex
Decreased volume of the basal ganglia structures

questions.explanation: The size of the amygdala is increased in depression and not decreased. Enlarged lateral ventricles have been found predominantly in the elderly with late-onset depression. Reduced hippocamapal volume is seen mainly in those with unipolar depression. Decreased volume of the basal ganglia structures is seen in those with unipolar depression. Decreased grey matter volume of the subgenual prefrontal cortex is seen in those with both unipolar and bipolar depression.

questions.question_text: Many risk factors have been identified for developing depressive disorders. Which ONE of the following statements regarding risk of developing depression is NOT true?

options.text: Risk is more increased in lower social classes than middle social classes following a life event
Risk is increased by having poor social support
Risk is increased if there is a first degree relative with bipolar affective disorder
Risk is increased in female heterosexuals compared to male homosexuals
Risk in single women doubles in the presence of poverty

correct_answer.text: Risk is increased in female heterosexuals compared to male homosexuals

correct_answers.text: Risk is increased in female heterosexuals compared to male homosexuals

questions.explanation: Research has documented consistently that persons of low-socioeconomic status (SES) are more strongly affected emotionally by undesirable life events than those of higher status. Studies examining sexual orientation and mental health have found a higher prevalence of anxiety, mood disorders, substance misuse and suicide in homosexual compared with heterosexual populations. Single mothers have twice the risk of developing depression and are twice as likely to have financial hardship. Having a first degree relative with bipolar disorder also increases your risk of developing unipolar depression.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following anatomical regions has NOT been shown to have altered cerebral blood flow and metabolism in studies of depressed patients using single-photon emission tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET)?
questions.explanation: No abnormalities of the hippocampus have been found on PET/SPECT scans of patients with depression. The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex is associated with cognitive dysfunction. The anterior cingulate is associated with impaired attention and abnormal emotional processing. The amygdala is associated with abnormal emotional processing. The basal ganglia are associated with impaired incentive behaviour and psychomotor disturbances.

questions.question_text: Early environmental influences might be involved in the aetiology of a depressive episode. Which ONE of the following has NOT been shown to increase the risk of developing depression in later life?
questions.explanation: Epidemiological studies do not suggest that the death of a parent in childhood increases the risk of depressive disorders in adult life. There is evidence that non-caring and overprotective parenting styles are associated with non-melancholic depression in adult life. Depressive disorders in later life are associated with parental separation, and especially divorce. There is a clear link between childhood sexual abuse and adult depression. Post-natal depression can lead to a parenting style characterised by neglect and emotional indifference, thus increasing the risk of depression in the next generation.

questions.question_text: A variety of neuro-endocrine abnormalities have been found in depressed subjects. Which of the following endocrine abnormalities has NOT been found in depression?

options.text: Blunted TSH response to i.v. TRH
Blunted response of Growth Hormone to Clonidine

questions.explanation: Free thyroxine levels are usually normal, but Clonidine-induced Growth Hormone response is blunted in depression. Elevated cortisol, GH and CRH are also seen in depression. A blunt TSH response is seen in one quarter of patients with depression, while T3 may be decreased.

questions.question_text: Life events (LE) have been implicated in the aetiology of many psychiatric disorders. Which ONE of the following statements about life events is NOT true?

options.text: LE are more likely to occur prior to relapse of mania
LE are more likely to cause depression when there is lack of a confidant
LE are less important before first episode of depression than in relapse
LE more likely to occur before depression than schizophrenia
LE are more likely to cause depression when they are exit rather than entry life events

correct_answer.text: LE are less important before first episode of depression than in relapse

correct_answers.text: LE are less important before first episode of depression than in relapse

questions.explanation: The relative risk of depression following life events is 6 compared with a relative risk of only 2 in schizophrenia. In general, the importance of life events in the onset of a depressive episode decreases as the number of episodes increases. The lack of a confidant was a vulnerability factor discovered by Brown and Harris (1978). Loss events are more common in depression. There is a small excess of life events prior to the relapse of mania.

questions.question_text: The dexamethasone suppression test (DST) suppresses cortisol via inhibition of ACTH at the pituitary level. Which of the following statements about DST is true?

options.text: Non-suppression is seen in patients with schizophrenia
Non-suppression is less likely in those with melancholia
DST has been used to provide evidence to support the monoamine theory of depression
It can be used to diagnose depression
There is non-suppression in over 90% of depressed subjects

correct_answer.text: Non-suppression is seen in patients with schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Non-suppression is seen in patients with schizophrenia

questions.explanation: The DST is not sensitive or specific enough to be used diagnostically in depression. There is non-suppression in only 50% of depressed patients - it is not a sensitive test. DST non-suppression is more frequently seen in patients with melancholia. DST is used to show evidence of HPA axis involvement and non-suppression is also found in mania and dementia.

questions.question_text: Genetic influences are acknowledged in the aetiology of mood disorders. Which ONE of the following has NOT been shown in studies examining the genetics of mood disorder?

options.text: Individuals with the short allele of the serotonin transporter gene polymorphism are more likely to become depressed following life events
The heritability of bipolar disorder is 85%
In bipolar disorder there is a susceptibility gene on chromosome 18 in some families
Relatives of unipolar probands have no increased risk of developing bipolar disorder
The risk of mood disorders in first degree relatives of those with bipolar disorder is increased 5-fold

correct_answer.text: The risk of mood disorders in first degree relatives of those with bipolar disorder is increased 5-fold

correct_answers.text: The risk of mood disorders in first degree relatives of those with bipolar disorder is increased 5-fold

questions.explanation: Twin studies at the Maudsley Hospital have revealed an 85% heritability for bipolar affective disorder. There is an approximately 2-fold increased risk of mood disorders in first degree relatives of those with bipolar disorder. Relatives of patients with unipolar disorder do not have increased rates of bipolar or schizoaffective disorders. A susceptibility gene on Chr 18 has been reported for bipolar disorder in genetic linkage studies. Association with the short allele of the 5HT transporter gene provides evidence of the gene-environment link in the aetiology of depression.

questions.question_text: The monoamine theory of depression suggests that depressive disorder is due to abnormality in the monoamine neurotransmitter system at one of more sites in the brain. Which ONE of the following neurochemical findings in depression supports this theory?

options.text: High levels of CSF homovanillic acid
Induction of depressive symptoms on administration of α-methyl-para-tyrosine (AMPT) in healthy subjects with a family history of depression

questions.explanation: There is reduced plasma tryprophan (the precursor amino acid to serotonin) and decreased platelet-5HT binding has been a finding in studies of the pathophysiology of depression. Low levels of 5-HIAA in CSF is a finding that is more specifically linked with impulsive or aggressive behaviour. AMPT is used to deplete noradrenaline; it has been shown to induce depressive symptoms only in patients with a past history of depression. Low levels of homovanillic acid, a dopamine metabolite are found in depression.

questions.question_text: Patients with depression show poor performance on several measures of neuropsychological function. Which ONE of the following domains has NOT been shown to be impaired in depression?
questions.explanation: There is no language impairment in depression. There is however impairment of executive function, attention and memory (both retrograde and anterograde).

questions.question_text: Beck described a number of illogical ways of thinking in depression, which he referred to as 'cognitive distortions'. Which ONE of the following distortions is NOT seen in depression?
questions.explanation: Repression is a defence mechanism described in psychoanalytic theory, and is not a cognitive distortion associated with depression. The others are examples of cognitive distortions seen in depression: Arbitrary inference is the phenomenon of drawing a conclusion when there is no evidence for it and some against it; Personalisation is the relating of external events to oneself in an unwarranted way; Selective abstraction implies focusing on the detail and ignoring more important features of a situation; Overgeneralization is the drawing of a general conclusion on the basis of a single incident.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a recognised symptom of severe depression?
questions.explanation: Most depressed patients experience difficulty in falling asleep, frequent awakenings during the night or awakening very early in the morning. The opposite, excessive sleeping, occurs in a minority of severely depressed patients. It can occur along with symptoms of 'atypical depression' which include increased appetite and weight gain. Atypical depression (reversed biological symptoms) often occurs along with excessive sensitivity to interpersonal rejection. Some authors claim that the diagnosis can be missed in favour of a personality disorder. There are also some claims that atypical depression responds better to MAOIs than to tricyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Normal bereavement is most likely to include which ONE of the following symptoms?

options.text: Delusional beliefs that the deceased is still alive

questions.explanation: It is important to point out that no single feature is pathognomic of abnormal grief and it is the intensity and duration of the features which determine the clinical picture. However, the presence of delusions would be abnormal; ideas of worthlessness and persistent guilt are also more likely to be associated with abnormal grief. In normal grief reaction the person loses appetite rather than significant weight. Anger is mostly directed towards the deceased or the world rather than the self.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following symptoms is NOT concordant with a diagnosis of mania?
questions.explanation: Clouding of consciousness suggests an organic cause. However, manic stupor and brief periods of depressed mood are recognised phenomenon in mania. Persecutory delusions are also well recognised in mania. First-rank symptoms have been reported in 10-20% of manic patients.

questions.question_text: The phenomenon of 'rapid cycling' has been described in bipolar affective disorder. Which ONE of the following statements about rapid cycling bipolar disorder is true?

options.text: It occurs more frequently in men
It commonly occurs earlier in the course of the illness
It is defined as at least six distinct episodes a year

questions.explanation: Concomitant hypothyroidism with rapidly cycling bipolar disorder is common. Four episodes in 1 year is the accepted definition. Rapid cycling occurs later in the course of illness and is seen at some stage of illness in 15% of patients. It is more common in females.

questions.question_text: Regarding the course of mood disorders, which ONE of the following statements is true?

options.text: Bipolar I has a better outcome than bipolar II
65% of depressed patients will have further episodes
Depressive episodes are shorter than Manic episodes
30% of patients with depression develop a chronic, unremitting course
90% of patients with mania have further episodes

correct_answer.text: 90% of patients with mania have further episodes

correct_answers.text: 90% of patients with mania have further episodes

questions.explanation: Both manic and depressive episodes (treated and untreated) last about 6 months. 80% will have further episodes, but only 10-20% develop a chronic, unremitting illness. The prognosis for mania is poorer than for unipolar depression, and bipolar II has a better outcome than bipolar I.

questions.question_text: Sleep changes are noted in depression. Which ONE of the following changes in sleep architecture has NOT been described in depression?

options.text: Decreased latency of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep
Increase in proportion of REM sleep in the early part of the night

questions.explanation: There is no reduction in fast-wave sleep (stage 2 sleep) in depression, but there is a reduction of slow wave sleep (sleep stages 3 and 4). There is impairment of both sleep continuity and duration. REM latency is shortened in depression and there is an increased proportion of REM sleep in the early part of the night.

questions.question_text: Both DSM-IV and ICD-10 classify mood disorders. Which ONE of the following statements regarding the classification of mood disorders is NOT correct?

options.text: Bipolar II disorder requires the presence of at least one hypomanic episode
In DSM-IV, manic episodes precipitated by antidepressants are not counted in the diagnosis of bipolar disorder
In ICD-10, the presence of a single episode of mania or hypomania is enough to meet the criteria for bipolar disorder
Depression is categorised according to severity in ICD-10
In DSM-IV, presence of a mixed affective state excludes bipolar II

correct_answer.text: In ICD-10, the presence of a single episode of mania or hypomania is enough to meet the criteria for bipolar disorder

correct_answers.text: In ICD-10, the presence of a single episode of mania or hypomania is enough to meet the criteria for bipolar disorder

questions.explanation: There must be at least two episodes of mood disturbance for the diagnosis of Bipolar disorder according to ICD-10. The diagnosis of Bipolar II disorder requires at least one hypomanic episode. There is some argument as to whether mania/hypomania induced by antidepressants should be taken as indicating an underlying bipolar disorder; in DSM-IV, mania or hypomania precipitated by antidepressants does NOT count towards a diagnosis of bipolar disorder. The presence of a manic episode or mixed affective state excludes bipolar II. Depression is categorised according to severity in both ICD-10 and DSM-IV.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used as a screening tool in psychiatry?
questions.explanation: The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) consists of 21 items which can be scored from 0-3. It is used to assess the intensity of depression in clinical and normal patients and has good sensitivity and specificity as a screening tool. The cut-off scores are: 0-13= minimal depression, 14-19= mild depression, 20-28= moderate depression, 29-63 severe depression.

questions.question_text: Epidemiological studies of Bipolar Disorder have shown which ONE of the following?

options.text: There is an increase of manic episodes in summer months
Female patients have proportionally more manic episodes than men
Age of onset is later than in unipolar disorder

correct_answer.text: There is an increase of manic episodes in summer months

correct_answers.text: There is an increase of manic episodes in summer months

questions.explanation: There is an increase of manic episodes in the summer months, although there is rarely a seasonal pattern of episodes within individual patients. Studies have shown that women tend to have fewer manic episodes, but prevalence is equal in males and females. The mean age of onset is earlier than of unipolar disorders, at 17 years. The lifetime risk is between 0.3-1.5%.

questions.question_text: Epidemiological studies of depression have shown which ONE of the following? Choose one answer

options.text: The gender difference becomes more exaggerated with increasing age
Age of onset is usually in late adolescence
Risk of major depression has increased over recent decades

correct_answer.text: Risk of major depression has increased over recent decades

correct_answers.text: Risk of major depression has increased over recent decades

questions.explanation: Studies have shown increased risk of depression over the last few decades. A recent WHO commissioned study reported in the Lancet in March 2008 reporst that depression will be the 2nd leading cause of morbidity worldwide by 2030. The gender difference in depression persists across the age range. The mean age of onset is 27 years. When socio-economic and education variables are controlled for, there is minimal evidence of racial or ethnic differences in the prevalence of depression.

questions.question_text: The following are recommended in the treatment of mild depression except:
questions.explanation: Antidepressants are not recommended in mild depression as the risk benefit ratio is poor.

questions.question_text: Which rating scale would you use to assess the response to antidepressants in a woman who has recently given birth and appears depressed?
questions.explanation: The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) is a 10-item self-rating post-natal depression scale which has seen widespread use in epidemiological and clinical studies.

questions.question_text: A range of psychotropics are used in the prophylactic treatment of bipolar disorder. Which ONE of the following statements about prophylactic treatment in bipolar disorder is NOT true?

options.text: Lithium is associated with reduced risk of suicide
Cognitive therapy has proven efficacy in the prevention of relapse
Carbamazepine and lithium combined are more effective than either drug alone
Olanzapine prevents more manic than depressive relapses
Carbamazepine is as effective as lithium

correct_answer.text: Carbamazepine is as effective as lithium

correct_answers.text: Carbamazepine is as effective as lithium

questions.explanation: Lithium has superior efficacy to carbamazepine. Olanzapine is more effective in preventing manic episodes. There is a link between lithium treatment and reduced suicide risk. There is evidence that cognitive therapy in bipolar disorder is effective in relapse prevention. The combination of these lithium and carbamazepine has superior efficacy than when they are used alone.

questions.question_text: Patients differ in their response to lithium therapy. Factors which predict a good response to lithium include which ONE of the following?

options.text: First episode of depression as opposed to mania

questions.explanation: A family history of bipolar disorder is strongly predictive of prophylactic efficacy. Neurological signs predict a poor response to lithium. Cases where the first episode was manic do better on lithium. Rapid cyclers respond poorly to lithium. Good inter-episode functioning is predictive of a good response.

questions.question_text: Which of the following options can be considered in the initial treatment of severe depression:
questions.explanation: The combination of antidepressants and individual CBT should be considered in the initial management as it is more cost effective than either on its own.

questions.question_text: A patient on Clozapine complains of abdominal pain and appears confused. The most likely explanation for his symptoms would be:
questions.explanation: Although up to 30% of patients on Clozapine may develop diabetes over 5 years, severe hyperglycemia, sometimes leading to ketoacidosis is rare. It has been reported in a number of case reports during Clozapine treatment in patients with no prior history of hyperglycemia.

questions.question_text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) has been associated with cognitive side effects. Which ONE of the following statements is NOT true about the effects of ECT on cognition?

options.text: Cognitive effects are increased with high doses of anaesthetic agents
Bilateral electrode placement produces greater impairment than unilateral
Anterograde amnesia is associated with more difficulties over the long-term than retrograde amnesia
Sine waveform is associated with increased cognitive impairment

correct_answer.text: Anterograde amnesia is associated with more difficulties over the long-term than retrograde amnesia

correct_answers.text: Anterograde amnesia is associated with more difficulties over the long-term than retrograde amnesia

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia is thought to cause more difficulties over the long-term than anterograde amnesia. The other statements are true: high-dose ECT produces greater impairment than low-dose; bilateral ECT produces greater impairment than unilateral ECT; sine waves are associated with increased cognitive impairment; high doses of anaesthetic are associated with adverse cognitive effects in ECT.

questions.question_text: The following drugs are recommended for post-stroke depression except:
questions.explanation: Mianserin seems ineffective, and SSRIs & Nortriptyline are recommended antidepressants for treatment of post stroke depression.

questions.question_text: Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) has been shown to respond to phototherapy. Which ONE of the following statements about phototherapy is true?

options.text: 70% of patients with SAD will respond to phototherapy
It is important that some skin is exposed to the light
Response is independent of the intensity of light

questions.explanation: Early morning phototherapy is superior but leads to increased side effects. About a half of patients have a clinically significant response to the treatment. Response is dependent on the intensity of the light. It is important for the eyes to be exposed as skin absorption does not alter circadian rhythms and is ineffective in SAD. The longer the duration of phototherapy, the better the response.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant of choice in a patient with recent history of MI or unstable angina is:
questions.explanation: The best evidence for antidepressant use in patients with cardiovascular disease is available for Sertraline.

questions.question_text: If depression has not responded to 2 adequate trials of different antidepressants the following can be considered
questions.explanation: All the above are options in the routine management of treatment ressitant depression

questions.question_text: A 40 year old woman with diagnosis of Bipolar Affective Disorder has had over the last few years four episodes of depression and one episode of hypomania. Which of the following drugs should be used as maintenance?
questions.explanation: The anticonvulsant Lamotrigine, recently approved as maintenance therapy for bipolar depression, has undergone evaluation as acute and maintenance therapy for bipolar disorder in several controlled clinical trials. NICE guidelines advocate the use of Lithium, Olanzapine, and valproate for prophylaxis of Bipolar disorder; Lamotrigine is recommended to be used in Bipolar II disorder and recurrent depression. Depression mood stabilisers, which stabilise mood from below the mood baseline (euthymia), without inducing switch into mania or episode acceleration, are useful for the treatment of bipolar depression.

questions.question_text: A man would like to take a herbal antidepressant. Which herbal antidepressant would you recommend?
questions.explanation: Although there is evidence that extracts of hypericum are more effective than placebo for the treatment of mild to moderately severe depressive disorders (see reference), these herbs have not been the subject of any rigorous trial and there are significant problems with interactions with other medications like warfarin and oral contraceptives. Serotonin syndrome is a possibility should the patient continue to take the prepartion along with a prescribed SSRI. These drugs are best avoided.

questions.question_text: The duration of maintence treatment with antidepressants in patients with more than two depressive episodes is:
questions.explanation: Patients with more than 2 depressive episodes should be advised to continue antidepressants for 2years.

questions.question_text: Many studies have examined the efficacy of antidepressant treatment in different situations. Which ONE of the following findings relating to antidepressant efficacy is NOT true?

options.text: Antidepressants are not effective in acute mild depression
Response to antidepressants is unrelated to prior life events
Tricyclics are more effective than SSRIs in hospitalised patients
Antidepressants are not effective in the treatment of dysthymia
Venlafaxine at doses of over 150mg/day is more effective than SSRIs in treating severe depression

correct_answer.text: Antidepressants are not effective in the treatment of dysthymia

correct_answers.text: Antidepressants are not effective in the treatment of dysthymia

questions.explanation: Antidepressants are effective in the treatment of dysthymia. Tricyclic antidepressants are more effective in hospitalised patients. There is some evidence that Venlafaxine is more effective at higher doses in treating moderate to severe depression. Antidepressants show no effect in acute mild depression. Response to antidepressants is unrelated to prior life events but response to placebo appears to be higher in those with prior life events.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following strategies is NOT advocated in the treatment of bipolar depression?
questions.explanation: Tricyclics are not recommended because of the risk of switching to mania. There is good evidence to support the use of lamotrigine in bipolar depression. CBT is effective and safe in bipolar depression. IPT is effective and safe in bipolar depression. Lithium can be used in the treatment of bipolar depression.

questions.question_text: A man comes to your clinic nine months after the death of his mother. He occasionally hears her voice calling him. You find features of a moderate depressive illness. Your best course of action is to:

options.text: Start an antipsychotic and follow him up
Do nothing and reassure him it will all go away
Start an antidepressant and follow him up.

correct_answer.text: Start an antidepressant and follow him up.

correct_answers.text: Start an antidepressant and follow him up.

questions.explanation: The differentiation between a normal grief reaction and depression/abnormal grief does not depend on any specific symptom. The symptoms of depression and abnormal grief are similar. It is the intensity and duration of the symptoms which are important in making the clinical differentiation. In this case it appears that the man is suffering from a prolonged grief reaction (moderate derpessive symptoms at 9 months post bereavement) and might benefit from antidepressant treatment.

questions.question_text: The first line of treatment for moderate-to-severe depression in the UK is
questions.explanation: SSRI's are as potent as TCA's and not likely to be discontinued

questions.question_text: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) is increasingly being used in the treatment of mood disorders. Which ONE of the following statements regarding the efficacy of CBT is TRUE?

options.text: There is no neurobiological basis for the efficacy of CBT
CBT is more effective than interpersonal therapy in the treatment of mild-moderate depression
Cognitive therapy is more effective than behavioural therapy
CBT is as effective as antidepressants in severe depression
When treatment is withdrawn, relapse rates are lower for CBT than antidepressants

correct_answer.text: When treatment is withdrawn, relapse rates are lower for CBT than antidepressants

correct_answers.text: When treatment is withdrawn, relapse rates are lower for CBT than antidepressants

questions.explanation: Relapse rates are less after withdrawal of CBT rather than antidepressants. CBT and IPT have been shown to have equal efficacy for mild-moderate depression. CBT is less effective than antidepressants in severe depression. PET studies have shown significant metabolic changes that are thought to underlie the effect of CBT. Cognitive therapy and behavioural therapy are equally effective.

questions.question_text: In relation to cannabis use and public health, which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Recent evidence suggests that cannabis use probably causes more harm to public health than tobacco or alcohol use.
Cannabis use appears to have dramatically increased since the recent reclassification of cannabis under the UK Misuse of Drugs Act.
Preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis.
If cannabis use does not cause psychosis then there is no public health justification for preventing cannabis use.
There is good evidence that the prohibition of cannabis use is an effective strategy to reduce use among young people.

correct_answer.text: Preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis.

correct_answers.text: Preventing cannabis use may lead to reductions in population rates of psychosis.

questions.explanation: Evidence of an association between cannabis use and psychosis has recently emerged. By normal epidemiological conventions, evidence that this association has a causal basis is currently not strong. However, cannabis may cause psychosis and this possibility presents a means to effectively reduce the population burden of illnesses such as schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Ketamine and phenylcyclidine can induce schizophrenia-like psychosis in humans. This provides evidence for the role of which neurotransmitter in the aetiology of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Ketamine and phenylcyclidine act as antagonists at the NMDA glutamate receptor. GABA, acetylcholine or dopamine transmission is not affected.

questions.question_text: With regard to cannabis use and psychotic illness in the UK population over the past 30 years, which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Only a small minority of young people today are likely to have used cannabis.
Rates of psychosis have clearly increased.
Rates of psychosis have clearly fallen.
Use of cannabis by young people has increased.
If cannabis use causes psychosis, increasing rates of cannabis use should have led to increasing rates of psychosis.

correct_answer.text: Use of cannabis by young people has increased.

correct_answers.text: Use of cannabis by young people has increased.

questions.explanation: In the UK around half of adolescents will use cannabis at least once and about a fifth of them will use it regularly (monthly or more frequently) in young adulthood. Cannabis is currently a Category C drug, however the home secretary has advised that is should be reclassified as a Category B drug from 2009. The reclassification reflects the market for cannabis in the UK being dominated by a more potent form of cannabis, skunk.

questions.question_text: Functional and structural neuroimaging has revealed a variety of differences in the brains of schizophrenics compared with healthy controls. Which ONE of the following brain abnormalities has been found in schizophrenia?

options.text: Increased volume of the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus
Reduced numbers of glutamate receptors in the frontal areas of the brain
Increased cerebral blood flow in the prefrontal cortex
Decreased expression of 5HT2A receptors in the prefrontal cortex

correct_answer.text: Decreased expression of 5HT2A receptors in the prefrontal cortex

correct_answers.text: Decreased expression of 5HT2A receptors in the prefrontal cortex

questions.explanation: The decreased expression of 5HT2A receptors in prefrontal cortex gives weight to the serotonin hypothesis of schizophrenia. Structural imaging studies consistently show reduced volume of hippocampus and parahippocampal structures. Glutamate receptors are increased in frontal areas and reduced in the medial temporal lobe. There is reduced blood flow in the prefrontal cortex indicating 'hypofrontality'. There is decreased brain weight compared with healthy individuals.

questions.question_text: An increased rate of schizophrenia-like psychosis has been observed in individuals with velocardiofacial syndrome (VCFS). Which candidate gene in the aetiology of schizophrenia has been implicated in VCFS?
questions.explanation: Velocardiofacial syndrome involves a microdeletion in chromosome 22 (deletion of 22q11); the COMT gene is found on 22q11.

questions.question_text: Individuals with Schizoptypy:

options.text: Are not considered as having a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder
Do not share common genetic vulnerabilities with schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Schizotypy is a concept which describes a continumm of personality characteristics and experiences related to psychosis, in particular schizophrenia. The characteristics include poor social interactions, unusual experiences (hallucinations, magical thinking, delusions), cognitive disorginsation, & non-conformity. Though this schizophrenia spectrum disorder is considered to share common genetic vulnerabilities, the relationship with schizophrenia is complex and not well understood.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following conditions has been associated with catatonia?
questions.explanation: Various neurotransmitter abnormailities have been reported in Catatonia, including reduced GABA & Dopamine, and increased Glutamate, Acetylcholine and Serotonin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding the genetics of schizophrenia?

options.text: Genetic evidence is inconsistent with the neurodevelopment hypothesis of schizophrenia
Genes involved in synaptic function determine susceptibility to schizophrenia.
Schizophrenia has a small genetic component.
Genetic studies do not support the concept of schizotaxia.
Genetic predisposition always leads to schizotypy or schizophrenia.

correct_answer.text: Genes involved in synaptic function determine susceptibility to schizophrenia.

correct_answers.text: Genes involved in synaptic function determine susceptibility to schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia and other schizophrenia-spectrum disorders are neurodevelopmental disorders which may share genetic susceptibility factors and represent different expressions of an underlying vulnerability. The relationship between spectrum disorders and schizophrenia is complex, with not all individuals who display characteristics of a prodrome going on to develop schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Genetic studies like linkage analysis and association studies have attempted to identify genes specifically associated with schizophrenia. Which ONE of the following has been strongly associated with susceptibility to schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Dysbindin (also known as dystrobrevin binding protein 1) is postulated to be a schizophrenia susceptibility gene. Located on chromosome 6p, it encodes a neural protein that binds to beta-dystrobrevin, which is located at pre-synaptic terminals and participates in signal transduction. BRCA-1 is a susceptibility gene for breast cancer. HNF4-alpha is a susceptibility gene for diabetes, and CHEK-2 is associated with predisposition to prostate and breast cancers.

questions.question_text: Research into schizophrenia has examined the unaffected relatives (who share some genetic material with the patient) in order to elucidate the aetiology of the disorder. Which ONE of the following has NOT been found in first degree relatives of schizophrenic patients?

options.text: A 10-fold increase in their risk of developing schizophrenia.
An increased risk of bipolar affective disorder.

correct_answer.text: An increased risk of bipolar affective disorder.

correct_answers.text: An increased risk of bipolar affective disorder.

questions.explanation: There is no increased risk of bipolar disorder in relatives of schizophrenia patients. There is a 10-20 fold increased risk of developing schizophrenia in siblings and offspring of patients, but the risk is lower in parents of schizophrenics. High-risk subjects had significantly reduced mean volumes of the left and right amygdala, hippocampus and thalamus when compared to healthy controls. The amplitude of the p300 wave (a measure of auditory information processing) is reduced in patients and a proportion of their first-degree relatives. 25% of first-degree relatives have defective performance in tests of eye tracking.

questions.question_text: Cognitive impairments in schizophrenia have been increasingly recognised using neuropsychological methods. They are associated with poor functional outcome. Which ONE of the following statements about neuropsychological abnormalities in schizophrenia is TRUE?

options.text: There are abnormalities in face recognition
They show no resolution with treatment of the acute episode

correct_answer.text: There are abnormalities in face recognition

correct_answers.text: There are abnormalities in face recognition

questions.explanation: Abnormalities in face recognition in schizophrenia may be related to dysfuction in the frontal cortex and amygdala. Schizophrenic patients are known to suffer from information processing deficits which can be detected in deficits of prepulse inhibition. Implicit memory is preserved. Cognitive impairments can partially resolve after resolution of the acute episode. Schizophrenic patients have been shown to have a number of cognitive deficits premorbidly, including lower premorbid IQ.

questions.question_text: If both parents of a child have schizophrenia, the risk of the child developing schizophrenia is?
questions.explanation: Risk of developing schizophrenia in children whose biological parents both have the disorder is 46.3%. If a single parent is affected the risk to the child is 6%. An indentical twin with the illness also confers a 46% chance whereas a sibling or dizygotic twin with the disorder confers a 10% risk of developing the illness for the proband. A sibling and a parent being affected brings the risk to 17%. Having a child with schizophrenia confers a 13% risk on the parent. And finally, having an uncle, aunt, nephew, or niece with the illness confers a 3-4% lifetime risk.

questions.question_text: With regards to schizophrenia in childhood which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Outcome of childhood-onset schizophrenia is better than that of adolescent onset schizophrenia
A diagnosis of schizophrenia does not have predictive validity
Interventions do not have any effect on measures of schizotypy in adult life.
Younger age correlates with higher thought disorder scores

correct_answer.text: Younger age correlates with higher thought disorder scores

correct_answers.text: Younger age correlates with higher thought disorder scores

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia and other schizophrenia-spectrum disorders are neurodevelopmental disorders which may share genetic susceptibility factors and represent differential expressions of an underlying vulnerability. The identification of prodrome (which includes features of spectrum disorders), could have impact of early interventions.The outcome of childhood onset schizophrenia is worse than adolescent onset schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Regarding the evidence that cannabis use may cause psychotic illness, which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: An increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions.
Confounding occurs when people exaggerate both their use of cannabis and their experience of psychotic symptoms.
Cannabis use is associated with increased diagnosis of schizophrenia.
It is likely that the association between cannabis use and psychotic symptoms seen in several studies has arisen by chance.
The fact that there are plausible neurophysiological mechanisms through which cannabis use might cause psychosis is probably the strongest evidence that it does.

correct_answer.text: An increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions.

correct_answers.text: An increased frequency of reported cannabis use has been associated with increased reporting of unusual thoughts and perceptions.

questions.explanation: Since the late 1960s cannabis use has increased substantially in most high-income countries (Hickman et al, 2007). The increase may now be levelling off, but this is hardly a reason for complacency. Cannabis is now well established as the third most widely used psychoactive drug (after alcohol and tobacco) in Europe, the USA and Australasia (Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs, 2006). In the UK around half of adolescents will use cannabis at least once and about a fifth of them will use it regularly (monthly or more frequently) in young adulthood.

questions.question_text: Development factors associated with schizophrenia ...

options.text: Do not include abnormal motor development.
Do not include poor social adjustment.

questions.explanation: The prevalence of schizophrenia in childhood is low, but children who develop schizophrenia in adult life may show subtle and non-specific developmental abnormalities, consistent with the neurodevelopmental hypothesis. These include motor, social, and cognitive (educational) difficulties. The neurodevelopmental influences can be early (peirnatal) or later (in childhood).

questions.question_text: Many psychosocial factors have been associated with the development of schizophrenia. Which ONE of the following psychosocial factors has NOT been shown to be associated with an increased risk of developing schizophrenia?

options.text: In adopted subjects whose biological parents have a personality disorder
Being born between July to September
Those who exhibit less social play as children

correct_answer.text: Being born between July to September

correct_answers.text: Being born between July to September

questions.explanation: Increased rates of schizophrenia have been found in those born in January to March. Increased rates of schizophrenia have been found in the offspring of women who suffered severe food deprivation during the first trimester. Low IQ is associated with birth trauma and neurodevelopmental impairment. It was found by Kety in the Danish adoption study that biological relatives had higher rates of DSM-III schizotypal personality disorder. Jones (1994) found that children who eventually developed schizophrenia showed delayed developmental milestones, speech problems, lower educational test scores and less social play.

questions.question_text: Many studies have attempted to explain the social correlates of schizophrenia. Which ONE of the following social factors has NOT been associated with increased risk of schizophrenia?

options.text: Being born into a socially deprived household

questions.explanation: There is a link between childhood sexual abuse and psychotic symptoms in later life, but a link with schizophrenia per se is not convincing. The first admission rate for schizophrenia is generally higher in urban than rural areas, and much higher from the central areas of large cities than from the surrounding suburbs. The relative risk for migrants is 2.7. Patients with schizophrenia are more likely to have been born into socially deprived households. Individuals who live in households where there is a high level expressed emotion from relatives (including critical comments) have a 2- to 3-fold increased risk of schizophrenia (as well as increased risk of relapse in those already with a diagnosis).

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following statements about primary negative symptoms in schizophrenia is NOT true?

options.text: They occur later in the illness.
They can be due to neuroleptic medication.
They are associated with structural abnormalities in the prefrontal cortex.
They are associated with poor prognosis.

correct_answer.text: They can be due to neuroleptic medication.

correct_answers.text: They can be due to neuroleptic medication.

questions.explanation: Secondary, but not primary negative symptoms may be related to medication. Primary negative symptoms occur late in the natural history of the illness. Structural abnormalities in the parts of the brain responsible for executive function are associated with negative symptoms; they indicate a poor prognosis. Affective blunting is one of the core features of the negative syndrome.

questions.question_text: According to ICD-10, which ONE of the following disorders is a recognised subtype of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Undifferentiated schizophrenia is a term used in ICD-10 to describe a syndrome which does not fit readily into any of the defined subtypes of schizophrenia. There is no category for paraphrenia or late-onset schizophrenia. Bouffee Delirante is now classified as an acute and transient psychotic disorder and hence resolves rapidly. Disorganised is an equivalent term for hebephrenic schizophrenia, which is used in DSM-IV. Deficit syndrome describes a syndrome with early severe and persistent negative symptoms.

questions.question_text: Cannabis has been highlighted, albeit controversially, as a potential causative factor in schizophrenia. Which ONE of the following has NOT been found in studies examining the link between cannabis use and schizophrenia?

options.text: If cannabis were eliminated, this could prevent approximately 25% of cases of schizophrenia.
It is more likely to cause psychosis in those who start using cannabis early.
There is a dose-response relationship to risk of developing psychosis.
Cannabis increases the relative risk of developing schizophrenia by up to 6 times.
It increases the release of dopamine.

correct_answer.text: If cannabis were eliminated, this could prevent approximately 25% of cases of schizophrenia.

correct_answers.text: If cannabis were eliminated, this could prevent approximately 25% of cases of schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Assuming a causal relationship, the elimination of cannabis use at the population level would reduce the incidence of schizophrenia by about 8%. The Swedish Conscript Study by Andreasson et al (1987) showed that the relative risk of developing schizophrenia is increased up to 6-fold in those with a history of heavy use of cannabis. This strengthens the argument for cannabis being a causative factor. Early onset of cannabis use confers the greatest risk. Elevation of dopamine levels is thought to be the mechanism by which cannabis can produce or exacerbate psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: With regards to the differential diagnosis of catatonia, which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: A functional or organic cause is always identifiable.
Increasing age is a risk factor for catatonic depression.
Catatonia associated with mood disorders is less common than catatonia associated with schizophrenia.
Idiopthic catatonia is more common in males.
Deep-vein thrombosis is a recognised cause of catatonia.

correct_answer.text: Increasing age is a risk factor for catatonic depression.

correct_answers.text: Increasing age is a risk factor for catatonic depression.

questions.explanation: Increasing age is a risk factor for catatonic depression. Catatonia is more commonly associated with mood disorders than with schizophrenia. Various causes of catatonia include infections, metabolic abnormality, cocaine, ciprofloxacilin, withdrawal of clozapine etc.

questions.question_text: Liddle (1987) defined 3 overlapping clinical syndromes in schizophrenia, which he linked to patterns of neuropsychological deficit and to regional cerebral blood blood flow. Liddle's clinical syndromes of schizophrenia included which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: Liddle examined the pattern of correlation between schizophrenic symptoms in a group of patients with illnesses of similar chronicity and found that the symptoms segregated into three distinguishable syndromes. Psychomotor poverty (poverty of speech, flat affect, decreased spontaneous movement), disorganisation (disorder of form of thought and inappropriate affect), and reality distortion (delusions and hallucinations).

questions.question_text: Kurt Schneider identified a group of experiences that might provide a reliable basis for the diagnosis of schizophrenia, known as 'first rank symptoms'. Schneider's first rank symptoms of schizophrenia: (choose ONE of the following)

options.text: Predict outcome of schizophrenia at 5 years.

questions.explanation: In the absence of cerebral pathology, the presence of any of Schneider's first-rank symptoms is indicative of, though not pathognomonic of, schizophrenia. The first-rank symptoms do not have prognostic significance. The first-rank symptoms are : auditory hallucinations (3rd person or thought echo or running commentary), thought alienation (thought insertion, broadcasting or withdrawal), somatic passivity, delusional perception, made feelings, impulses or actions.

questions.question_text: The presence of high levels of which ONE of the following is most strongly linked to transition to psychosis?
questions.explanation: The factors that predict the transition to psychosis of at risk individuals include positive symptoms, low GAF scores (poor functioning), and depression. Mania, anxiety or negative symptoms were not different between the group who made the transition to psychosis and the group which did not.

questions.question_text: The outcome of a case of schizophrenia is remarkably heterogeneous and unpredictable. Features associated with a worse prognosis in schizophrenia include which ONE of the following?
questions.explanation: Structural brain abnormalities have been linked with worse outcomes in schizophrenia. Prominent affective symptoms are associated with a better prognosis. Interestingly, research shows that the outcome is better in those living in developing countries. A clear precipitant is linked with a better outcome. Acute onset is linked with a better prognosis.

questions.question_text: People are thought to be at risk of developing psychosis if:

options.text: Their ability to function has deteriorated over the previous 2 months
They experience frank psychotic symptoms, which remit within a week
They experience subclinical symptoms, which remit within a week
They have a relative with a diagnosis of a psychotic disorder
They meet the criteria for schizotypal personality disorder

correct_answer.text: They experience frank psychotic symptoms, which remit within a week

correct_answers.text: They experience frank psychotic symptoms, which remit within a week

questions.explanation: Some highly significant predictors of psychosis were found in a study by Yung et al 2003 for predicting who develop psychosis in a high risk group. The predictors include: long duration of prodromal symptoms, poor functioning at intake, low-grade psychotic symptoms, depression and disorganization.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is NOT CONSISTENT with a diagnosis of persistent delusional disorder?

options.text: Presence of symptoms for at least 3 months

questions.explanation: The presence of a first-rank symptom (thought insertion) would suggest schizophrenia. According to ICD-10, in order to make a diagnosis of persistent delusional disorder, the symptoms must have been present for at least 3 months. Transitory (not persistent) hallucinations can occur in delusional disorders. There is evidence that deafness (but not blindness) is associated with delusional disorder. The mean age of onset for delusional disorders is 42 years.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following statements about suicide in schizophrenia is NOT true?

options.text: It is associated with high premorbid functioning
It is most likely to occur later in the illness
It can be reduced by clozapine treatment
It accounts for up to 40% of the excess mortality in schizophrenia
There is a lifetime risk of 7%

correct_answer.text: It is most likely to occur later in the illness

correct_answers.text: It is most likely to occur later in the illness

questions.explanation: Suicide usually occurs earlier in the illness. Risk of death from suicide is increased 10-fold in schizophrenia. The lifetime risk is approx 7%. High premorbid functioning is associated with increased suicide risk in schizophrenia. An RCT by Meltzer et al (2003) showed clozapine treatment significantly reduced suicide risk.

questions.question_text: There are important gender differences in several aspects of schizophrenia and its treatment. Which ONE of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Schizophrenia in women is associated with later onset
Schizophrenia in women shows a bimodal peak of incidence
Schizophrenia in women has a slightly lower incidence than in men
Schizophrenia in women is associated with more structural brain abnormalities than men
Schizophrenia in women is associated with lower mortality compared with men

correct_answer.text: Schizophrenia in women is associated with more structural brain abnormalities than men

correct_answers.text: Schizophrenia in women is associated with more structural brain abnormalities than men

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia in men is associated with more structural brain abnormalities. The incidence of schizophrenia is slightly higher in men than in women. There is a later mean age of onset in women (5 years later) and a second peak around 50 years. The mortality rate in men with schizophrenia is twice that of women.

questions.question_text: Many epidemiological studies have examined the patterns of prevalence of schizophrenia. Which ONE of the following statements about the prevalence of schizophrenia is accurate?

options.text: The prevalence of schizophrenia is 2.3% during a lifetime, according to the Epidemiologic Catchment Area Study
The prevalence of schizophrenia is similar across different populations
The prevalence of schizophrenia is low, relative to its incidence
The prevalence is higher in Barbados than in the UK
Prevalence is higher in developing than in developed countries

correct_answer.text: The prevalence of schizophrenia is similar across different populations

correct_answers.text: The prevalence of schizophrenia is similar across different populations

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia has a low incidence but relatively high prevalence. Prevalence rates are broadly similar across populations; for example in Africa, India and Western countries. Incidence rates for schizophrenia in the Caribbean are similar, hence the concern over higher rates in Afro-Caribbean populations in England. Low prevalence of schizophrenia has been reported in the Hutterites and the Anabaptist sect in the USA. The ECA is a popular subject for factual statements; the lifetime prevalence of schizophrenia was found to be 1.3%

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following has been shown to be effective in reducing the risk of developing psychosis in at-risk mental states?
questions.explanation: Either low dose antipsychotics or a combination of low dose antipsychotics with cognitive therapy is advocated by some for management of at-risk individuals; ethical issues however need to be considered since not all of the at-risk population go on to develop psychosis.

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following is TRUE regarding the treatment of catatonia?

options.text: NMDA agonists have role in treatment
Carbamazepine is contraindicated in the acute catatonic phase
Clinically significant improvement typically begins to occur about 24 hours after starting medications
ECT is indicated in both functional and organic catatonia
Antipsychotics are the first line treatment

correct_answer.text: ECT is indicated in both functional and organic catatonia

correct_answers.text: ECT is indicated in both functional and organic catatonia

questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are the first line treatment, and ECT is used if BZD treatment fails. Other treatments that can be used are Mood stabilisers (Carbamazepine), NMDA antagonists, Dopamine agonists. Antipsychotics are at best avoided during the acute catatonic phase. Improvement, though dramatic in few, takes up to 48 hours to be seen during treatment with benzodiapines.

questions.question_text: Clozapine is the only antipsychotic licensed for use in treatment resistant schizophrenia. Clozapine treatment:

options.text: Would be expected to cause little postural hypotension, judging by its receptor binding profile
Causes more akathisia at any clinical dose than risperidone
Causes hypersalivation by interaction with muscarinic M3 receptors
May be used with carbamazepine for those experiencing clozapine-induced seizures

questions.explanation: Clozapine is the only antipsychotic that is associated with alleviation of TD. It induces less akathisia than risperidone. It is thought that clozapine may produce hypersalivation though M4 agonism, alpha2 antagonism or inhibition of the swallowing reflex. Significant postural hypotension is a common sideeffect of clozapine hence the very slow dose titration on initiation. The combination of clozapine and carbamazepine is dangerous due to the potential for blood dyscrasias.

questions.question_text: After one episode of schizophrenia, antipsychotics should be continued for:
questions.explanation: Recommended for 1-2 years after a first episode of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A proportion of schizophrenic patients do not respond adequately to conventional treatment and are defined as 'treatment resistant'. Which ONE of the following statements regarding treatment-resistant schizophrenia is TRUE?

options.text: It is a situation where antipsychotic polypharmacy may be recommended
It is more likely in those with predominantly positive psychotic symptoms
It is defined as lack of clinical improvement despite the sequential use of the recommended doses for 6 to 8 weeks of at least 3 antipsychotics
It responds to clozapine in approximately 60% of patients
It occurs in approximately 1/4 of patients

correct_answer.text: It is a situation where antipsychotic polypharmacy may be recommended

correct_answers.text: It is a situation where antipsychotic polypharmacy may be recommended

questions.explanation: Although antipsychotic polypharmacy should generally be avoided, TRS is one situation where it can be used with some benefit. The NICE Guidelines state that treatment-resistance occurs after adequate trial with only 2 antipsychotics, one of which should have been an atypical. Approximately 30% of patients do not respond to antipsychotics. It is more likely in those with more negative symptoms. Studies have shown that approximately 30% of patients with TRS will respond to clozapine.

questions.question_text: Regarding psychosocial interventions in schizophrenia, which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Cognitive remediation is a treatment for positive psychotic symptoms
CBT is effective in the treatment of delusions
Presence of high expressed emotion within families predict the outcome of most psychiatric disorders
Compliance therapy has not yet been shown to improve the outcome of patients prescribed neuroleptic medication
Intensive case management has been shown to be more effective than other therapies in preventing relapse in psychoses

correct_answer.text: CBT is effective in the treatment of delusions

correct_answers.text: CBT is effective in the treatment of delusions

questions.explanation: The efficacy of CBT in schizophrenia is well established. The benefits of compliance therapy were reported by Kemp in 1996. The UK700 trial did not find an advantage for intensive case management except in some specific subgroups of patients. Cognitive remediation is a treatment for cognitive impairment in schizophrenia. Expressed emotion has primarily been implicated in the relapse of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a rare but fatal complication of antipsychotic treatment. Which ONE of the following statements about NMS is NOT true?

options.text: It is more likely to occur in those where physical restraint has been used
The risk of recurrence is 30 times greater following one episode
NMS can be treated with bromocriptine

questions.explanation: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome can occur at any dose. Physical restraint is a risk factor for NMS. Leukocytosis is commonly found on routine blood investigations. The finding that risk of recurrence is 30 times greater following one episode of NMS was demonstrated by Gurrera (2002). Treatment can include administration of a dopamine agonist.

questions.question_text: The following are options for augmenting clozapine in a patient who has shown partial response to clozapine treatment, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Pimozide is not recommended due to cardiotoxicity.

questions.question_text: A female schizophrenia patient has been put on Olanzapine and Quetiapine, but with poor effect. Your next step is to try:
questions.explanation: After a trial of two antipsychotics, of which at least one must be a second generation antipsychotic, it is reasonable to switch to clozapine, if possible. This guidance from NICE is also presented as an algorithim in the Maudsley Guidelines

questions.question_text: Which ONE of the following statements about Clozapine is INCORRECT?

options.text: Is used for first-line treatment of Schizophrenia
Is very effective in actively and floridly psychotic patients

correct_answer.text: Is used for first-line treatment of Schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Is used for first-line treatment of Schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Clozapine is recommended after adequate trials of two different antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: Atypical antipsychotic medications are used in the first-line treatment of schizophrenia. Olanzapine is one example of an atypical antipsychotic drug. Which ONE of the following statements about olanzapine is TRUE?

options.text: It exerts its sedative effects through its 5HT2A receptor activity
It only causes diabetes mellitus at doses above 20mg
It has superior efficacy compared with haloperidol
It is less likely to cause hyperprolactinaemia than risperidone
Its association with more weight gain and metabolic effects when compared with other atypicals is not supported by research

correct_answer.text: It is less likely to cause hyperprolactinaemia than risperidone

correct_answers.text: It is less likely to cause hyperprolactinaemia than risperidone

questions.explanation: The atypicals risperidone, amisulpiride and zotepine are more potent D2 antagonists and therefore have the highest risk of inducing hyperprolactinaemia. In the CATIE study, olanzapine was associated with greater weight gain and increases in measures of glucose and lipid metabolism. The available data do not indicate a clear difference in efficacy between typicals and atypicals, apart from clozapine. Olanzapine does not require high doses to be associated with diabetes mellitus. The sedative effects of olanzapine are because of its potent antihistaminergic effects.

questions.question_text: There is growing interest in the idea that early treatment of schizophrenia may improve the long-term outcome. Which ONE of the following statements about early intervention in psychosis is TRUE?

options.text: The mean DUP (duration of untreated psychosis) is 1-2 years
Prolonged DUP correlates with neurobiological markers of illness severity
Advocates use of high-dose antipsychotics early in the illness
Out of those found 'at risk' of developing psychosis in the PACE study, 80% became psychotic within one year
The 'critical period' refers to the period of brain development during childhood when environmental damage can lead to psychotic symptoms in adulthood

correct_answer.text: The mean DUP (duration of untreated psychosis) is 1-2 years

correct_answers.text: The mean DUP (duration of untreated psychosis) is 1-2 years

questions.explanation: The mean duration of untreated psychosis is 1-2 years, and is true even in countries with highly developed systems of healthcare. The 'critical period' refers to the 3-5 year period following illness onset when there may be a decline in social and cognitive function. Only 40% developed psychosis in the first year. Prolonged duration of untreated psychosis does not correlate with neurobiological markers of illness severity, which may indicate that prolonged DUP may not be a direct causal link with poor outcome. Low-dose atypicals are used.

questions.question_text: CBT for delusions is contraindicated if the patient:

options.text: Is not distressed by their paranoia

correct_answer.text: Is not distressed by their paranoia

correct_answers.text: Is not distressed by their paranoia

questions.explanation: CBT is recommended for people with distressing symptoms as it enables individuals to engage with the collaborative goal of reducing distress; hence it is not recommended for people who are not distressed by their symptoms. CBT has been shown to be effective in treatment of persistent symptoms, particularly delusions. Poor insight, cognitive deficits, and taking medications are not contraindications.

questions.question_text: Tardive dyskinesia refers to involuntary, choreoathetoid movements of (typically) the orofacial structures. Which ONE of the following findings related to tardive dyskinesia is NOT true?

options.text: May increase on cessation of antipsychotic treatment
Is more likely to occur in older patients
Is more likely to occur in those with a family history of Parkinson's disease
Is associated with Gly/Gly allele of the DRD3 gene
May occur through activation of D3 receptors

correct_answer.text: May occur through activation of D3 receptors

correct_answers.text: May occur through activation of D3 receptors

questions.explanation: It is thought that TD occurs due to dopamine D2 receptor hypersensitivity (and not D3). Stopping antipsychotics sometimes worsens the movement disorder. A family history of Parkinson's disease is a known risk factor for developing TD. Increasing age is a risk factor for TD. Studies have shown increased allelic frequency of the serine-glycine substitution in the DRD3 gene that codes for the D3 receptor.

questions.question_text: The antipsychotic which is best supported for use in patients with Tardive Dyskinesia is:
questions.explanation: Clozapine has the best evidence for use in Tardive Dyskinesia; however, there is also  evidence emerging for Quetiapine and Olanzapine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following causes symptoms of inappropriate ADH secretion?
questions.explanation: Hyponatraemia can occur due to drug-induced SIADH. All the antipsychotics listed (olanzapine, haloperidol, quetiapine, risperidone) and several others have been implicated. Regular sodium monitoring is desirable. The Maudsley prescribing guidelines, 9th Edition, 2007, p138.

questions.question_text: A male schizophrenia patient on clozapine has gained 20kg. Your next step is to:
questions.explanation: Aripiprazole seems to have the least effect on weight gain. Clozapine and Olanzapine have the highest risk, followed by zotepine, chlorpromazine, quetiapine and risperidone (moderate risk), and amisulpride, aripiprazole, haloperidol, trifluoperazine and ziprasidone (low risk).

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old university student presents with persecutory ideas, sadness and inability to concentrate. His academic performance had deteriorated recently which he put down to a plot hatched by the aliens and his tutors at the university to stem the growth of the genius in him. He also mentioned hearing people laughing at him when alone select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation: This is paranoid schizophrenia, characterised by a prodrome and presence of persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations.

questions.question_text: After six months of treatment with antipsychotic medication, he recovered well and started to go back to the university, although not totally convinced about his tutors. He developed a low mood, difficulty in concentration, increasing tiredness and inability to sleep. He lost weight and had recurrent worries about death. select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation: This is post-psychotic depression. Note that this can only be diagnosed once the psychotic symptoms are absent or present minimally.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old man believes that his suffering is the greatest in the world. He has been feeling low for 6 weeks and lost a lot of weight from not eating, as he believes that all his intestines were rotten and he couldn‘t digest any food even if he tried to eat. He has lost all interest and motivation to do anything.
questions.explanation: The coexistence of depressive symptoms and mood congruent delusions suggests psychotic depression.

questions.question_text: An older schizophrenic woman has developed diabetes mellitus. She is agreeing to take medication but has irregular compliance with tablets and is currently psychotic. When her son reminds her to take her tablets they usually end up in a quarrel. Choose a treatment for clinical presentations
questions.explanation: In this scenario a depot antipsychotic would be most appropriate to ensure compliance and manage her psychosis.

questions.question_text: An elderly man with persistent psychotic symptoms, he is not tolerating oral flupentixol. He has previously failed to respond to sulpiride and olanzapine. Choose a treatment for clinical presentations.
questions.explanation: This describes treatment resistance. In this case, clozapine would be the medication of choice.

questions.question_text: A woman with Parkinson‘s disease, troubled by hallucinations. She is not currently on an antiparkinsonian drug and is antipsychotic naïve. Choose a treatment for clinical presentations
questions.explanation: According to the Maudsley Prescribing guidelines, quetiapine at lower doses can be used to treat psychotic symptoms in Parkinson‘s disease.

questions.question_text: which three of the below are risk factors for suicide.
questions.explanation: Living alone, past psychiatric history and recent discharge from psychiatric hospital are risk factors for suicide.

questions.question_text: which three of the below are risk factors for depression.
questions.explanation: Female sex, living alone (in the context of poor social support) and past history are risk factors for depression.

questions.question_text: which three of the below are risk factors for depression.
questions.explanation: There is a preponderance of females with late-onset schizophrenia (M:F = 7:1), premorbidly patients tend to have poor adjustment, social isolation and lower marriage and childbearing rates and sensory impairment is also over-represented.

questions.question_text: A 44 year old homeless man is brought into A&E. He is agitated, psychotic and depressed. The ECG shows decreased alpha activity and his gait is disturbed. MRI shows hypointensity of the striatum.
questions.explanation: DT can present as vivid hallucinations, delusions, profound confusion and inattention, agitation and restlessness, sleeplessness, autonomic overactivity and fearful affect. Gait can be disturbed, EEG might show reduced alpha activity and MRI could reflect changes in striatum.

questions.question_text: A 25 year old man recently returned from America shows aggressive behaviour. He recently has periods of decreased consciousness associated with making funny movements with his hands and sounds from his lips. His full blood count and liver functions are normal.
questions.explanation: Complex partial seizures cause impaired consciousness and arise from a single brain region. Impaired consciousness implies decreased responsiveness and awareness of self and surroundings. During a complex partial seizure, the patient may not communicate, respond to commands, or remember events that occurred. Epilepsy of prolonged duration and brain dysfunction involving a broad area including the temporal and frontal lobes may be associated with the occurrence of subacute postictal aggression.

questions.question_text: A 30 year old woman has one sided facial nerve palsy and circumscribed lesions on both legs.
questions.explanation: Shingles is an acute infection caused by reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus. After primary chickenpox infection, the virus lies dormant in the dorsal root ganglia of the spinal cord. When reactivated, it travels along the sensory nerve to affect one or more dermatomes, causing the characteristic shingles rash. It can lead to complications like Ramsay Hunt syndrome characterised by unilateral facial palsy associated with pain and herpetic blisters in the external auditory meatus due to involvement of the geniculate ganglion.

questions.question_text: A 30 year old woman has had two episodes of depression and one episode of mania in the last eight months. She has been compliant with her mood stabiliser medication, which she has been on for the last ten years. She is currently depressed and has taken an overdose of her tablets two days ago. identify the most indicated investigations.
questions.explanation: A lithium level would be useful to check for potential toxicity, possibly related to overdose and also to check whether the levels are within therapeutic range, as low levels may indicate noncompliance and possible relapse. The rapid cycling nature of her disorder warrants a thyroid function test.

questions.question_text: A 73 year-old lady was brought by her son. She had a six-month history of being withdrawn, reduced appetite and self-care. She had occasionally, mentioned about suicidal ideas to her son and all her symptoms had worsened over six weeks, after the death of her husband. She has been on antihypertensive medication for over 10 years. identify the most indicated investigations.
questions.explanation: Informant history is vital to assess this lady. MMSE would screen for a dementia and TFTs would rule out underlying hypothyroidism.

questions.question_text: A 47-year-old man with a long history of alcohol and opioid dependence was admitted after he had attempted to hang himself. On assessment he was found to be more depressed subjectively rather than objectively.
questions.explanation: Blood gases are important to check for hypoxia and acid-base disturbance. An informant history would also be useful as would a narcotic drug screen, given the history of opioid dependence.

questions.question_text: An elderly woman has insomnia, low mood and weight loss. She tells you there is no point in her eating anything as her insides are rotting.  select the most appropriate diagnosis.
questions.explanation: Cotards syndrome is used to describe nihilistic delusions occurring within a depressive episode. These delusions characteristically involve ideas of the bowels rotting away, although other ideas such as being dead, part of the body being rotten can also be seen. It is often, although not exclusively, seen in older people with severe depression. It can also occur in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder & organic conditions involving lesions in the non-dominant temporoparietal cortex.

questions.question_text: A young man whose wife is pregnant complains of morning sickness and an inflated abdomen. select the most appropriate diagnosis.
questions.explanation: Couvade Syndrome is the term used to describe a man who is experiencing symptoms of his partner‘s pregnancy. Various theories have been suggested to explain this although none are conclusive. questions.question_text: A 50-year-old man develops nodules on the shin and also respiratory problems. Choose ONE option.
questions.explanation: Neurosarcoidosis is a serious and devastating manifestation of sarcoidosis in the nervous system. Sarcoidosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder that typically occurs in adults between 20 and 40 years of age and primarily affects the lungs, but can also impact almost every other organ and system in the body. Histologically, neurosarcoidosis is characterized by formation of granulomas in the central nervous system. The lesion consists of lymphocytes and mononuclear phagocytes surrounding a noncaseating epithelioid cell granuloma. These granulomas represent an autoimmune response to central nervous system tissues.

questions.question_text: Select the rating scales that are useful for the scenarios described. To assess symptoms of depression in a 37 year old lady presenting for the first time to psychiatric services.

options.text: Scale for Negative symptoms in schizophrenia

questions.explanation: The Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAM-D, HRSD) is the most widely utilized rating scale to assess symptoms of depression. The HAM-D is an observer-rated scale consisting of 17 to 21 items (including two 2-part items, weight and diurnal variation). Ratings are made on the basis of the clinical interview, plus any additional available information, such as nursing or family member report. The items are rated on either a 0 to 4 spectrum (0 = none/absent and 4 = most severe) or a 0 to 2 spectrum (0 = absent/none and 2 = severe). The HAM-D heavily emphasizes somatic symptoms of depression and works best for the assessment of individuals with relatively severe illness. The Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) is a frequently used observer-rated depression scale. The scale was developed more than 20 years ago but is still favourite among researchers to measure the severity of depressive disorders and the changes of depressive symptoms during therapy.
